ir_definition: "the ratio between the majority class and each of the minority classes"; Table 1 IR = Majority instances / Minority instances

chosen.table: Table 2 (mean CV score across 69 datasets); Table 3 (mean rank); Table 5 (Holm adjusted p)
chosen.classifier: LR (first reported; abstract highlights no classifier)
chosen.condition: all 69 datasets, 5-fold CV repeated 3 times, best hyper-parameters

summary_rows.label: Holm adjusted p-value vs SMOTE, G-SMOTE control (Table 5, LR, G-MEAN)

outcome.stat_test: Friedman test (alpha 0.05) + Holm's method with G-SMOTE as control (Tables 4-5, p.23)

win_claim.quote: We present empirical results that show a significant improvement in the quality of the generated data when G-SMOTE is used as an oversampling algorithm.

uncertain: source_repo per dataset: paper says 13 UCI + 13 KEEL + 2 MANDELON (p.18) but Table 1 lists 27 distinct base names (13+13+2=28) and does not map each to a repository

how_obtained of base datasets set to 'not stated': names like YEAST 1/3/4/5/6, NEW THYROID 1/2, PAGE BLOCKS 0, PAGE BLOCKS 1 3 look like KEEL splits, and IRIS/WINE/GLASS/VEHICLE etc. must have been binarized, but the paper does not say (p.18)
MANDELON 1/2 marked synthetic: 'Simulated data based on variations of the MANDELON dataset' - unclear whether authors generated them or used NIPS 2003 MADELON as is (p.18)
Table 1 total of variants not verified against stated rule; listed exactly as printed (69 rows)
Classifier choice LR = first in Table 2; no classifier highlighted in abstract (p.21)
notes: No per-dataset results in paper; only means across datasets (Table 2), mean ranks (Table 3), Friedman (Table 4) and Holm (Table 5) for LR/KNN/DT/GBC x AUC/F-SCORE/G-MEAN. Full per-dataset results stated to be at https://github.com/IMS-ML-Lab/publications/blob/master/data/results/gsmote-journal/wide_optimal.csv (p.22, not fetched). Datasets at https://github.com/IMS-ML-Lab/research-showcase/tree/master/data/binary-numerical-imbalanced (p.18). Name printed as 'MANDELON' (sic, MADELON). G-MEAN other classifiers G-SMOTE vs SMOTE means: KNN 0.821/0.783, DT 0.866/0.833, GBC 0.868/0.834 (Table 2). Hyper-parameter special cases (SMOTE, inverse SMOTE, hyper-sphere SMOTE etc.) analysed in Fig.18 only. Table text extracted cleanly (not images).
